title: Call signals: shift log and triage hypotheses - May 09 2029
content:
TL;DR
- Quiet weekend overall, small noisy regression Friday evening tied to KV-cache evictions for the p99 model path.
- One pager incident (INC-2029-0421) opened, triage done, mitigation = temporary cache size bump + routing to fallback variant.
- SLOs slightly degraded for inference-hosted-api (p95 latency drift from 120ms -> 160ms during the spike). Error budget now ~64%.
- Action: short autotune run on cache thresholds, increase alerting granularity for cache-pressure metric, and add a runbook snippet for model-variant fallback.

Incidents (summary)
1) INC-2029-0421 — KV-cache eviction storm (resolved -> monitoring)
   - Time window: 2029-05-03 18:12 -> 2029-05-03 19:05 UTC
   - Impact: p95/p99 latency for hosted text-generation up to 3x baseline; 1.8% elevated 5xx on the edge for ~40min
   - Root-cause hypothesis: sudden increase in long-sequence requests caused frequent KV cache churn on the 80-A pool; eviction thrash plus improper metric tagging made autoscaler slow to react.
   - Mitigation applied: manual cache-size bump on 80-A pool, temporarily routed non-critical tenants to 60-B pool (fallback variant), tightened autoscale threshold for cache_pressure.
   - Postmortem notes: working draft in JIRA SRE-1842. Need to validate whether kernel-selection heuristics caused oversized memory working set.

2) Minor: Synthetic-test runner panic during deploy (5/06 03:20 UTC)
   - Caused by a flaky test harness container; not customer-facing. Flaky test ticket opened and moved to qa-flakes backlog.

SLO posture (current snapshot)
- inference-hosted-api availability target: 99.95% (rolling 30d) — current: 99.92%
- p95 latency target (short-gen endpoints): < 150ms — measured: 160ms (spike window), baseline otherwise ~118ms
- error budget remaining (30d): ~64% (down from 72% last week)
- Notes: trending risk is concentrated around longer sequence workloads we started onboarding. If sequence-length distribution shifts further we expect additional pressure on memory and p99 latency.

Observability and alerts
- New alert created: infra/cache_pressure.p95 > 0.7 for 3m -> SRE on-call (JIRA: SRE-1840)
- Existing alert tuning: lowered threshold for model-serving autoscale_cpu to trigger scale-up quicker; need to monitor false positives.
- Dashboards updated: added a split by seq_len_bucket on token-aggregation dashboard (see PR #542).

On-call handoff notes (for incoming shift)
- Primary focus: watch cache_pressure and model-variant routing ratios for 80-A and 60-B pools between 17:00-23:00 UTC (histor peak).
- If p95 > 200ms and cache_pressure > 0.8: follow incident playbook excerpt -> increase pool cache by +20% (safe patch), enable fallback routing rule for low-priority tenants, page infra-scaling channel.
- Contact list: Miguel (infra lead) mobile: +1-555-0133, Lena (runtime) slack: @lena_f
- Quick checks: recent deploys (deploy-2029-05-03) might correlate; roll history shows a canary on 80-A at 18:05 UTC (confirm whether rollback happened).

Runbook / Playbook fragments (working ideas)
- Fallback flow: if model-serving(p99) > 500ms for >10m and error_rate >1% -> flip routing for <enterprise-tier traffic to variant-v1-quantized, keep enterprise on pinned-capacity.
- Safe cache bump: perform via infra playbook to increment cache size on specific pool, then observe heap pressure for 5m. If heap crosses 85% -> revert and escalate to runtime.
- Observability patch: add cache_pressure per-tenant aggregated metric to avoid noisy aggregate signals.

Action items (owners and ETA)
- Aisha: run an autotune sweep on cache thresholds for long-sequence workloads (ETA: 2029-05-14)
- Miguel: validate kernel-selection logs for 80-A during the incident window and open infra PR for safer defaults (linked PR #542) (ETA: 2029-05-11)
- Lena: add runbook snippet and test fallback routing in staging (ETA: 2029-05-12)
- Tomiko: add seq_len_bucket sampling to synthetic load harness to reproduce eviction thrash (ETA: 2029-05-16)

Open questions and follow-ups
- Did the sequence-length distribution change because of one customer onboarding or an app-level bug? (CS: reach out to account engineering to correlate new tenants.)
- Are our autoscaler metrics consistent across cloud regions? Early signals show the eu-west pools behaved differently during the same window. Need cross-region diff.
- Should we introduce a lightweight token-prefix cache to reduce KV-cache pressure on long sequences? Pros/cons list needed.

Notes to self / raw scribbles
- observe: cache_pressure spikes correlate with increased token-window retention on KV cache; maybe LRU eviction policy not optimal for our prefix-heavy workload.
- thought: consider a tiered cache (short-prefix LRU + long-prefix LFU?) — prototype idea in infra/experiments.
- TODO: schedule 30m sync with product for tenant onboarding flow (ask: are they converting many short->long prompts?).

Links & references
- JIRA: SRE-1842 (incident draft)
- JIRA: SRE-1840 (alert tuning)
- Slack: #sre-bridge thread 2029-05-09 (contains immediate triage chatter)
- GitHub: infra PR 542 (dashboard + autoscaler tweak)

Bottom line: not critical yet but heading toward a repeatable pressure pattern once sequence-lengths increase. Short-term mitigations applied and owners assigned. Need to tighten observability and finalize fallback runbook before next traffic peak.

-- Aisha (on-call author)
